newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish transport group CIE sees 1.0 mln profit.
newsitem.headline: Irish transport group CIE sees 1.0 mln profit.

text.p: Irish transport group Coras Iompair Eireann (CIE) said it recorded a surplus of 1.0 million Irish pounds before an exceptional provision of 57 million in 1996.

"We have provided for the implementation of viability plans in the accounts," group chairman Brian Joyce said in a results statement. "Without this provision of 57 million the group would have made a small surplus of 1.0 million punts."
Joyce said the improved financial performance indicated that the company was beginning to turn the corner in its bid to achieve full commerciality.
CIE said customer revenues increased by 2.0 percent to 336 million Irish pounds in 1996 but said the challenge now facing the group was to grow revenue at a faster pace.
"The ability to earn a better return on our operations in the future is affected by the measures which are taken to tackle Ireland's worsening traffic gridlock problem," Joyce said.

He estimated the cost of the gridlock in Dublin alone at more than 1.0 billion punts per annum "... which is approximately 10 times the annual subvention which has been given to CIE for the provision of national transport services," Joyce said.
